correctness.rationale: For all k≥1, the cube sequence satisfies a monic order-four integer recurrence, so the GCD of all window shifts equals gcd(initial window, four consecutive boundary differences). The latter is reduced by exact expansion to gcd(F_k³,F_{k+1}³−1,3F_k gcd(F_k+F_{k+1},2)). Cassini and doubling identities give the base factor H(k), with an additional 3 exactly when 8|k; the telescoper 2∑F_j³=1−F_{k+1}³+3F_kF_{k+1}²−3F_k³ removes a factor 2 precisely when 6|k. Every parity/prime-power case is covered. The executable independently passed 8,400 finite shifted-window comparisons for k≤300; these are checks, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 paper arXiv:2204.12626 frames the higher-power problem as Question 6.1 and provides conjectural, not proved, cubic cases. The new theorem covers all window lengths and proves the corrected factor pattern. The 2021 first-power GCD paper and the 2017 cubic-sums paper do not imply the full simultaneous cubic-window GCD theorem by their stated results. Searches for direct and equivalent formulations disclosed no complete prior theorem; implicit/unindexed coverage remains possible.

value.rationale: This solves the mathematically motivated extension to powers three raised in Question 6.1 of arXiv:2204.12626, including all odd and even window lengths, with a closed Fibonacci/Lucas expression. The sharp exceptional local factors clarify the divisor structure in an infinite family and are not routine numerical table entries; the four-difference method gives a structural argument.
